seo.title: What Mexico, the EU, China & India Charge on U.S. Soda Ash and Chemicals (HTS 28) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Tariffs on U.S. soda ash, caustic soda, silicon and rare-earth compounds in 10 markets: free in Mexico, Canada, the EU and Korea; China adds 10%; India eyes quotas.
keywords: india soda ash anti dumping duty

intro: Four of the ten largest markets charge nothing on qualifying U.S. inorganic chemicals: **Mexico** and **Canada** under USMCA, **South Korea** under KORUS, and the **EU**, which cut every Chapter 28 duty to zero on July 1, 2026. Japan (up to 5.4%), the UK (up to 4%), Brazil (up to 10%), Viet Nam and India (mostly 7.5%) charge their normal rates, and **China** adds a 10% extra duty, with its older counter-tariffs on top unless the buyer holds an exclusion. The product-specific costs are trade remedies: Mexico's US$195-per-tonne anti-dumping duty on liquid caustic soda, China's 123.4% duty on hydriodic acid, South Africa's 40% duty on soda ash and, if India notifies it, a soda ash import quota. For most of these goods the buyer's chemical registration (REACH, K-REACH, Japan's Chemical Substances Control Law) matters more than the tariff; each market's regulator is listed below.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

assumptions: Each cell uses one representative six-digit subheading per heading: the one with the largest 2025 U.S. exports (for example 2836.20 soda ash, 2815.12 liquid caustic soda, 2804.61 silicon, 2844.10 natural uranium, 2843.90 precious-metal compounds, 2846.90 rare-earth compounds other than cerium). Other lines in the same heading can pay different rates.

MFN rates are World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) applied rates for 2023, the latest year WITS holds for these markets; a range means the market splits the subheading into national lines with different rates. National 8–10-digit lines and later schedule changes can differ.

Mexico (USMCA), Canada (CUSMA) and South Korea (KORUS) charge 0% only on goods that meet the agreement's rules of origin; the normal-rate column shows what a non-qualifying U.S. good would pay, including Mexico's decree of April 23, 2026, which raised its general rate on soda ash, calcium chloride and sodium bicarbonate to 35% and on furnace carbon black and sodium cyanide to 25%.

The EU cells apply Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, which sets 0% on all of Chapter 28 for goods of U.S. origin (non-preferential origin rules) from July 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029; the normal-rate column shows the EU common external tariff that applied before.

China's cells add the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods to China's rate, using the 2026 provisional rate where Tariff Commission Announcement No. 11 of 2025 sets one (rare-earth compounds, natural uranium, ammonia, alumina, iodine, boric acid, borax). China's 2018–2019 counter-tariffs (Announcement 2019 No. 3, and the August 2019 list of Announcement 2019 No. 4, halved from February 14, 2020 by Announcement 2020 No. 1) are named in each basis but not added, because importers can apply for exclusions, valid until December 31, 2026.

India's cells show the basic customs duty only; the Social Welfare Surcharge and IGST are not included. Trade-remedy duties are named in the basis where they reach the representative subheading (Mexico on liquid caustic soda, China on hydriodic acid); VAT and other internal taxes are not included.
